topics_covered.title: 1.4 File Directory Structure
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Absolute paths vs relative file paths, directory trees, path separators (\ vs /), and navigating folders via GUI and Command Prompt.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.
key_points: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.
topics_covered.explanation: Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

topics_covered.title: 1.4 File Directory Structure
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Absolute paths vs relative file paths, directory trees, path separators (\ vs /), and navigating folders via GUI and Command Prompt.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.
key_points: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.
topics_covered.explanation:
### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Absolute paths vs relative file paths, directory trees, path separators (\ vs /), and navigating folders via GUI and Command Prompt.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].

topics_covered.title: 1.5 File Conversion, Importing and Exporting
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Converting document, image, and media formats (e.g., DOCX to PDF, XLSX to CSV) and importing/exporting data across applications.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

book-10-it_ch_1_topic_file_directory_str.detailed_overview:
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

Key Takeaway: The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

topics_covered.title: 1.4 File Directory Structure
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Absolute paths vs relative file paths, directory trees, path separators (\ vs /), and navigating folders via GUI and Command Prompt.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.
key_points: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Absolute paths vs relative file paths, directory trees, path separators (\ vs /), and navigating folders via GUI and Command Prompt.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

topics_covered.title: 1.5 File Conversion, Importing and Exporting
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Converting document, image, and media formats (e.g., DOCX to PDF, XLSX to CSV) and importing/exporting data across applications.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Converting document, image, and media formats (e.g., DOCX to PDF, XLSX to CSV) and importing/exporting data across applications.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

```text

Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Converting document, image, and media formats (e.g., DOCX to PDF, XLSX to CSV) and importing/exporting data across applications.

- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

```text

This section provides an analytical examination of fundamental definitions, theoretical mechanisms, empirical formulas, and practical applications aligned with the official Ethiopian Ministry of Education curriculum.

topics_covered.title: 2.1 Network Media (Transmission Media)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Guided (wired) media: UTP/STP twisted-pair (RJ-45), coaxial cable, and fiber-optic cable (single-mode/multi-mode); Unguided (wireless) media: radio waves, microwaves, and infrared.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

topics_covered.title: 2.1 Network Media (Transmission Media)
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Guided (wired) media: UTP/STP twisted-pair (RJ-45), coaxial cable, and fiber-optic cable (single-mode/multi-mode); Unguided (wireless) media: radio waves, microwaves, and infrared.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.
key_points: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).

The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Guided (wired) media: UTP/STP twisted-pair (RJ-45), coaxial cable, and fiber-optic cable (single-mode/multi-mode); Unguided (wireless) media: radio waves, microwaves, and infrared.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

book-10-it_ch_2_topic_telecommunications.detailed_overview:
### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Components of telecommunications systems, analog vs digital signals, modulation/demodulation, multiplexing, and bandwidth/throughput.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| **Governing Law** | The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via... | Formulated per MoE Guidelines |
| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Cellular architecture (cells, base transceiver stations, mobile switching centers, handoff) and evolution from 1G, 2G (GSM), 3G, 4G (LTE) to 5G.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** TCP/IP protocol suite, IPv4 (32-bit dotted decimal, classes, public vs private) vs IPv6 (128-bit hexadecimal), subnet mask, DNS, and DHCP.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Unit Overview

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Unit Overview
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Advanced document publishing, data analysis, and visual presentation in office suites.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Slide Master customization, action buttons, hyperlinks, embedding audio/video, animation pane timing, rehearsal, and speaker notes.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Unit Overview
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Advanced document publishing, data analysis, and visual presentation in office suites.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Advanced document publishing, data analysis, and visual presentation in office suites.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Unit Overview
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Advanced document publishing, data analysis, and visual presentation in office suites.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Creating and formatting complex tables, inserting pictures/shapes/SmartArt, section breaks, multi-column layouts, automatic Table of Contents (TOC), citations, and Mail Merge.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].

Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

topics_covered.title: 3.2 Word Processing
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Creating and formatting complex tables, inserting pictures/shapes/SmartArt, section breaks, multi-column layouts, automatic Table of Contents (TOC), citations, and Mail Merge.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

book-10-it_ch_3_topic_spreadsheet__detai.detailed_overview:
### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Relative ($A1), absolute ($A$1), and mixed cell references; advanced functions (IF, COUNTIF, SUMIF, VLOOKUP, RANK, AND, OR); data sorting, filtering, conditional formatting, and charts.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```


| Parameter / Aspect | Academic Specification & Meaning | National Syllabus Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Topic** | 3.3 Spreadsheet | Unit 3 Framework |
| **Governing Law** | The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via... | Formulated per MoE Guidelines |
| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

Key Takeaway: The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

topics_covered.title: 3.3 Spreadsheet
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Relative ($A1), absolute ($A$1), and mixed cell references; advanced functions (IF, COUNTIF, SUMIF, VLOOKUP, RANK, AND, OR); data sorting, filtering, conditional formatting, and charts.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Slide Master customization, action buttons, hyperlinks, embedding audio/video, animation pane timing, rehearsal, and speaker notes.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

topics_covered.title: 3.4 PowerPoint Presentation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Slide Master customization, action buttons, hyperlinks, embedding audio/video, animation pane timing, rehearsal, and speaker notes.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

topics_covered.title: 4.1 Basics of Multimedia
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Linear vs non-linear (interactive) multimedia, hypertext vs hypermedia, and hardware/software requirements for multimedia systems.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Linear vs non-linear (interactive) multimedia, hypertext vs hypermedia, and hardware/software requirements for multimedia systems.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```


| Parameter / Aspect | Academic Specification & Meaning | National Syllabus Standard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Topic** | 4.1 Basics of Multimedia | Unit 4 Framework |
| **Governing Law** | The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via... | Formulated per MoE Guidelines |
| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

topics_covered.title: 4.4 Multimedia Editing
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Image editing (layers, masks, curves, healing brush, clone stamp), audio editing (trimming, noise reduction, mixing), and non-linear video editing (timeline, transitions, chroma key).

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

topics_covered.title: 5.1 Information and Computer Security & Impact on Society
topics_covered.topic_title: 5.1 Information and Computer Security & Impact on Society
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: National critical infrastructure protection, digital trust, e-banking/e-government security, and societal implications of cyber incidents.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** National critical infrastructure protection, digital trust, e-banking/e-government security, and societal implications of cyber incidents.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Topic** | 5.1 Information and Computer Security & Impact on Society | Unit 5 Framework |
| **Governing Law** | The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via... | Formulated per MoE Guidelines |
| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

topics_covered.topic_title: 5.1 Information and Computer Security & Impact on Society
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: National critical infrastructure protection, digital trust, e-banking/e-government security, and societal implications of cyber incidents.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Advanced malware (ransomware, rootkits, keyloggers, botnets), social engineering (phishing, spear-phishing, pretexting), SQL injection, and Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

topics_covered.title: 5.3 Computer Security Threats
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Advanced malware (ransomware, rootkits, keyloggers, botnets), social engineering (phishing, spear-phishing, pretexting), SQL injection, and Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

topics_covered.title: 5.4 Threat Prevention Strategies
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Technical controls: encryption (symmetric & public-key), firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), VPNs, patch management, and biometric access control.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.

Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

book-10-it_ch_5_Threat Prevention Strate.detailed_overview:
### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Technical controls: encryption (symmetric & public-key), firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), VPNs, patch management, and biometric access control.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **Governing Law** | The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via... | Formulated per MoE Guidelines |
| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

topics_covered.title: 5.4 Threat Prevention Strategies
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Technical controls: encryption (symmetric & public-key), firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), VPNs, patch management, and biometric access control.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

book-10-it_ch_5_topic_cyber_security__de.detailed_overview:
### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Cyber defense frameworks, ethical hacking vs black-hat cracking, incident response, and Ethiopian Computer Crime Proclamation.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Core Topic** | 5.5 Cyber Security | Unit 5 Framework |
| **Governing Law** | The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via... | Formulated per MoE Guidelines |
| **Examination Traps** | Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), di... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

topics_covered.title: 5.5 Cyber Security
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Cyber defense frameworks, ethical hacking vs black-hat cracking, incident response, and Ethiopian Computer Crime Proclamation.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

book-10-it_ch_6.detailed_overview: Detailed curriculum study of Unit 6: Fundamentals of Programming (Grade 10 Information Technology). This section provides an analytical examination of fundamental definitions, theoretical mechanisms, empirical formulas, and practical applications aligned with the official Ethiopian Ministry of Education curriculum.

topics_covered.title: 6.1 Basics and Definition of Algorithm
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Role of algorithms in computer science, translating real-world logic into unambiguous computational instructions.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.
key_points: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 1. Unit Masterclass: Theoretical Foundations & Governing Laws
Unit 6 (Unit 6: Fundamentals of Programming) forms a foundational pillar of the Ethiopian Grade 10 Information Technology syllabus. It develops students' analytical rigor, linking fundamental physical and scientific laws to mathematical formulations and real-world systems.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Role of algorithms in computer science, translating real-world logic into unambiguous computational instructions.

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
- **Key Principle**: An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
- **Key Principle**: The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Von Neumann Computer Architecture: [Input Devices (Keyboard, Mouse)] ──> [CPU: CU + ALU + Registers] ◄──► [Primary Memory (RAM)] ──> [Output Devices (Monitor, Printer)].
```

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

Frequent in EUEE: converting binary to decimal numbers (e.g. 1010_2 = 10_10), distinguishing RAM vs ROM properties, identifying network topologies (Star, Bus, Ring), and malware definitions.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

topics_covered.title: 6.2 Characteristics of Algorithm
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Finiteness, definiteness (unambiguity), input, output, effectiveness, and generality of a valid algorithm.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

topics_covered.title: 6.1 Basics and Definition of Algorithm
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Role of algorithms in computer science, translating real-world logic into unambiguous computational instructions.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.

book-10-it_ch_6_Characteristics of Algor.detailed_overview:
Information Technology powers modern digital computation. The Von Neumann architecture coordinates CPU processing, high-speed RAM caching, and network protocols to process, transmit, and secure global digital information.

Key Takeaway: The CPU (ALU + CU) processes data stored in RAM; networking connects systems via TCP/IP protocols.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Ethiopia's Digital 2025 Strategy drives national fiber-optic broadband expansion, Ethio Telecom 5G rollout, and Telebirr digital mobile payment integration.

topics_covered.title: 6.2 Characteristics of Algorithm
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Finiteness, definiteness (unambiguity), input, output, effectiveness, and generality of a valid algorithm.

• Computer Hardware Architecture: Central Processing Unit (CPU) containing Control Unit (CU) and Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU). Primary Memory: RAM (Random Access Memory - volatile, temporary working memory) vs. ROM (Read Only Memory - non-volatile, contains BIOS boot instructions). Secondary Storage: HDD, SSD, USB flash drives.

• Data Measurement Units: Bit (0 or 1), Byte (8 bits), Kilobyte (KB = 1024 Bytes), Megabyte (MB), Gigabyte (GB), Terabyte (TB), Petabyte (PB). Binary system (Base-2) represents all digital numbers and text.

• System Software vs. Application Software: System Software: Operating Systems (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android) that manage hardware resources and provide user interface. Application Software: End-user productivity programs (word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers).

• Computer Networks & Internet Architecture: Network types: LAN (Local Area Network, e.g. school computer lab), MAN (Metropolitan), WAN (Wide Area Network, e.g. Global Internet). Devices: Routers, switches, modems. Protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS (translates domain names to IP addresses).

• Cyber Security & Digital Safety: Threats: Malware (Viruses, Worms, Trojans, Ransomware), Phishing scams, unauthorized intrusion. Protection: Strong passwords, two-factor authentication (2FA), firewalls, and regular data backups.
key_points: RAM loses all data when power is turned off (volatile); ROM and secondary storage retain data permanently (non-volatile).
An IP address uniquely identifies a device on a network (e.g. 192.168.1.1); DNS converts human-readable URLs (ethiolearn.et) into numeric IP addresses.
The ALU performs all mathematical calculations (+, -, *, /) and logical comparisons (<, >, ==) in the CPU.
